correctness.rationale: Decompose L2 over the affine intervals. A diagonal block is a restricted unnormalized Hilbert transform times the n-th power of the local slope, so its norm is at most pi times L to the n. Between two distinct ordered intervals, Lipschitz control majorizes the kernel by L to the n divided by distance; after choosing a separator this is a restricted Carleman kernel, whose L2 norm is pi by the standard weighted Schur calculation. The finite block matrix contributes at most the factor N.

final_claim: If a one-dimensional Lipschitz profile has N affine pieces, then its n-th Calderón commutator has L2 operator norm at most pi times N times the n-th power of the Lipschitz constant, uniformly in n apart from that natural exponential factor.
limitations: One-dimensional piecewise-affine profiles with fixed finite corner count only.
Does not rule out infinitely cornered profiles or corner counts growing with n.
